mediaWork.title: A Crime on the Bayou
mediaWork.publisherOrNetwork: Augusta Films, Get Lifted Film Company, Artemis Rising Foundation (Distributed by Shout! Studios)
mediaWork.focusOrTheme: Tells the story of Gary Duncan, a Black teenager arrested in 1966 in Plaquemines Parish, Louisiana, for touching a white youth's arm while trying to de-escalate a confrontation. Chronicles his challenge against the segregated justice system, aided by young Jewish attorney Richard Sobol, leading to the landmark Supreme Court case *Duncan v. Louisiana*.
mediaWork.summaryNotes: A Black teenager bravely challenges the most powerful white supremacist in 1960s Louisiana with the help of a young Jewish attorney. Systemic racism and the confederate statues are explored.

featuredIndividuals.narrativeSummary: Gary Duncan was wrongfully prosecuted and initially convicted of simple battery. His fight led to the landmark Supreme Court ruling in *Duncan v. Louisiana*, guaranteeing the right to a jury trial in state courts for serious crimes. It is unclear if his sentence was served before or during appeals.
